sections.title: Overview
bullets: Overview of Robotics Artificial Intelligence and Robotics • Artificial intelligence is the science of training machines to perform human tasks.
A robot has the following essential characteristics: o Sensing o Movement o Energy o Intelligence • Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics (1942): 1.
A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm.
A robot must obey orders given it by human beings except where such orders would conflict with the First Law.

sections.title: Key concepts
bullets: A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law.
History of Robotics • The main era of robotic research and development was the mid- 20th century.
Robots were mainly employed for tasks that were too dirty, distant or dangerous for humans (Krebs & Volpe, 2013).

Unimate is the first industrially used robot developed by Joseph Engelberger and George Devol in 1961, a 2-ton robotic arm adopted for automated die-casting (a metal casting process utilizing metal molds or dies).
Shakey developed by Charles Rosen in 1966, is the first mobile robot with the ability to perceive and reason about its surroundings.
The Stanford Arm is the first successfully computer-controlled electrically powered robot arm created by Victor Scheinman in 1969, developed industrial assembly techniques for commercial robot arms.

handouts.title: Simple Machines Fundamentals
handouts.summary: Simple Machines Fundamentals • A simple machine is a basic mechanical device for applying a force and doing work. Robots are made up of simple machines that allow them to perform actions.

sections.title: Overview
bullets: Simple Machines Fundamentals • A simple machine is a basic mechanical device for applying a force and doing work.
Robots are made up of simple machines that allow them to perform actions.
Types of simple machines: o Lever - is made up of a straight rigid object which pivots on a turning point to move or lift an object.
The parts of a lever as are follows: ▪ Bar or Beam – a long plank.

sections.title: Key concepts
bullets: (Seesaw) ▪ Class 2: The load is between the effort and the fulcrum.
(Wheelbarrow) ▪ Class 3: The effort is between the load and the fulcrum.

It uses a wheel with a rod attached in the middle as an axle to help it to lift or move loads.
Examples: Doorknob, motor, electric fan o Pulley – uses a wheel with a groove in it and a rope.

handouts.title: Microcontrollers Fundamentals
handouts.summary: Microcontrollers Fundamentals • A microcomputer typically consists of a microprocessor (CPU) chip, input and output chips, and memory chips in which programs (instructions and data) are stored. A microprocessor is the CPU of a microcomputer contained in a single chip and must be interfaced with memory and I/O chips in order to function.

sections.title: Overview
bullets: Microcontrollers Fundamentals • A microcomputer typically consists of a microprocessor (CPU) chip, input and output chips, and memory chips in which programs (instructions and data) are stored.
A microprocessor is the CPU of a microcomputer contained in a single chip and must be interfaced with memory and I/O chips in order to function.
A microcontroller is implemented in a single chip containing a CPU, memory, and IOP (I/O and peripherals).
A typical IOP contains an I/O unit, timers, AD (Analog-to-Digital) converter, and other peripheral functions.

sections.title: Key concepts
bullets: The basic blocks of a microcomputer are as follows: o Central Processing Unit (CPU) – executes all the instructions and performs arithmetic and logic operations on data.
Read-Only Memory (ROM) - retains its content when the power is turned off (non-volatile).
It is typically used to store instructions and data that do not change.
Random Access Memory (RAM) – does not retain its content when the power is turned off (volatile).
It is used to store programs and data that are temporary and might change during the course of executing a program.
Input/output (I/O) – transfers data between the microcomputer and the external devices via I/O ports (registers).

Microcontroller ? A single chip containing a CPU, memory, and input/output peripherals.
Central Processing Unit ? The component that executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logic operations on data.
ROM ? Read-only memory that retains its contents when power is off and stores fixed instructions and data.

handouts.title: Microcontroller Programming Fundamentals
handouts.summary: Microcontroller Programming Fundamentals • Programs written using Arduino Software (IDE) are called sketches, saved with the file extension, .ino. The Arduino programming language can be divided into three (3) main parts: functions, variables and constants, and structure.

sections.title: Overview
bullets: Microcontroller Programming Fundamentals • Programs written using Arduino Software (IDE) are called sketches, saved with the file extension, .ino.
The Arduino programming language can be divided into three (3) main parts: functions, variables and constants, and structure.
Functions are used for controlling the Arduino board and performing computations.
There are two (2) special functions that are required in every Arduino sketch: setup() and loop().

sections.title: Key concepts
bullets: It is used for tasks like setting pin modes or initializing libraries.
Some of the most commonly used functions in a sketch: o The pinMode() function configures a pin as either an input or an output.
To use this, indicate the number (or variable name) of the pin to configure and the constant, INPUT or OUTPUT.
pinMode(13, OUTPUT); o The digitalWrite() functions outputs a value on a pin.
To use this, indicate the number (or variable name) of the pin and the constant, HIGH or LOW.
digitalWrite(13, HIGH); o The delay() pauses the program for the specified number of milliseconds before continuing to the next line.

sections.title: Key terms
bullets: Sketch ? An Arduino program written in the Arduino IDE and saved with the .ino extension.
setup() ? The Arduino function called once when a sketch starts, used to set pin modes or initialize libraries.
loop() ? The Arduino function that executes statements repeatedly and is considered the heart of a sketch.
pinMode() ? The Arduino function that configures a pin as an input or an output.
digitalWrite() ? The Arduino function that outputs a HIGH or LOW value on a pin.
